A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GEM research work. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original GEM segmentation experiments, ablations, parameter-budget analyses, and measured inference costs in Section 4 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds qualitative segmentation comparisons in Appendix C, Figure 5.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same spatial convolutional adapter, latent-token context adapter, residual updates, and token-sharing procedure. The method equations and components are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate ScanNet, ScanNet200, ScanNet++, S3DIS, SemanticKITTI, and ShapeNetPart, retaining limited-data and indoor-to-outdoor settings. Figure 5 adds indoor segmentation examples without introducing a new dataset or distinct task requirement.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–10 and the prompt-tuning attention comparison remains unchanged. Figure 5 visualizes results against the already evaluated linear-probing baseline.

E3.justification: Reported splits, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, default rank 32, four latent tokens, and batch-one inference measurements are unchanged. Figure 5 does not document an altered evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds Figure 5: seven qualitative segmentation comparisons covering apartments, living rooms, and offices/lounges, examining clutter-region errors and object boundaries. Existing attention visualizations, ablations, and budget analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Results remain presented as point estimates, with no change in uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 and existing figure results are unchanged. Figure 5 adds segmentation predictions, and Appendix C newly reports cleaner, more coherent segments, fewer clutter-region confusions, and sharper boundaries relative to linear probing.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), adapter definitions, and computational-complexity arguments are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: geometry-aware adaptation through spatial and context adapters, approximately 1.6% trainable parameters, and performance competitive with full fine-tuning.

C2.justification: The mechanism interpretations and limitations concerning parallelization, large batches, and backpropagation through dense point clouds are retained. Appendix C adds qualitative observations without introducing a new causal explanation or applicability qualification.

D1.justification: Implementation and access information remain unchanged, including the Pointcept foundation, code links, single 4090 GPU, ScanNet training for 100 epochs, and inference benchmarking details. No additional reproduction instructions accompany Figure 5.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds five references, v3 references 47–51, on weak supervision, label efficiency, and boundary learning to contextualize data demands and specialized training objectives. All 93 earlier references are retained; the central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to the related-work paragraph, Appendix C, and a Figure 3 cross-reference. References change from alphabetical to citation order, with corresponding citation renumbering and compression. The overall narrative and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the multipart Figure 5 with input, ground-truth, baseline, GEM, and improvement columns. Figures 1–4 and Tables 1–10 retain their displays; the new figure and reordered bibliography cause localized layout changes.

improvement.justification: Figure 5 supplements v2's attention visualizations and aggregate scores with direct prediction-versus-ground-truth comparisons, making segmentation errors easier to inspect. Section 2 also gains relevant research context. These provide a limited improvement in evidence and explanation; the method, quantitative validation, and stated limitations remain unchanged.
